title: Tenant-aware tail-latency adaptive SLO and rollout playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As Redwood scales, tenant-specific traffic patterns create divergent tail latency behavior. One-size-fits-all P99 targets lead to excessive conservative throttling or noisy false positives. This PRD defines an adaptive per-tenant tail-latency SLO layer plus a staged rollout/playbook for applying SLO-driven mitigations without impacting availability for unaffected tenants. Goals: 1) Define measurable per-tenant latency SLOs (p95/p99) with dynamic baselining and weight adjustments. 2) Create explicit burn-rate and mitigation gates for canary, ramp, and full rollout. 3) Provide contract tests and CI gating to prevent deployments that regress tenant SLOs. 4) Implement observability dashboards and automated playbooks to execute failover/fallback and traffic shaping when burn thresholds are hit. Scope: Hosted API and Dedicated; excludes on-prem private installs in initial phase. This ticket covers SLO definitions, acceptance criteria, gating rules, observability requirements, and rollout plan. Implementation tasks live in ENG-38902 (SLO evaluation service), ENG-39211 (admission controller), and ENG-39560 (dashboards & alerts).
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant baseline computed from 28-day rolling window and stored as tenant_slo_baseline(metric = p99_latency_ms) in SLO service
Default SLO tiers applied when tenant-specific baseline is insufficient: 99th percentile <= 1200ms (tier-1), 99th percentile <= 2000ms (tier-2), otherwise tier-3
Adaptive SLO permits +/- 25% short-term deviation but triggers burn-rate analysis if deviation persists beyond 1 hour
Burn-rate policy: burn-rate > 2 for 30m -> automated canary rollback ramp block; burn-rate > 4 for 10m -> immediate traffic shaping and notify oncall
Canary gating: any deploy that increases global p99 by >3% or increases >3 tenants' p99 by >10% must fail CI and require manual approval
Dashboards: per-tenant p95/p99 time-series, burn-rate heatmap, top-20 offending endpoints, and canary probe results available in Console with 14d retention

Automated mitigations: (a) fallback to quantized/low-cost model variant for affected tenant, (b) progressive rate limit applied per tenant with exponential backoff, implemented by admission controller
Runbook: documented steps for oncall to escalate, apply manual shunt, and postmortem templates stored in Drive link below
Contract tests: PRs must include SLO regression tests that simulate a synthetic traffic pattern and assert no tenant-level p99 regression beyond defined thresholds
Telemetry: every mitigation action must emit an audit event with tenant_id, action, reason, and related deployment id
notes: Trade-offs: per-tenant adaptive SLOs improve signal but add complexity in billing/alerts; initial rollout will be limited to tenants with >10k daily requests to reduce noise
Decision: exclude private on-prem in Phase 1 to avoid needing customer-managed telemetry export; plan Phase 2 with opt-in telemetry agents
Performance considerations: SLO evaluation should run asynchronously and must not add >5% CPU to runtime control plane; ENG will implement sampling for high-throughput tenants
Fallback model variants: product to sign-off acceptable quality degradation thresholds for quantized variants before enabling automatic fallback
Operational overhead: we will create a new 'SLO incidents' channel and pre-authorized escalation list to avoid pager fatigue from transient burns

implementation_plan: Phase 0: Prototype SLO evaluator using historical traces (ENG-38902) - 2 weeks
Phase 1: Canary rollout to internal tenants and tier-1 customers with >10k daily requests (ENG-39211, ENG-39560) - 3 weeks
Phase 2: Expand to all hosted API tenants and Dedicated clusters, enable automatic mitigations and CI gating - 4 weeks
Rollback plan: automated disablement of adaptive SLO layer via feature flag; emergency manual shunt by oncall using Console route override
risks: False positives for small tenants causing unnecessary throttling - mitigated by minimum traffic threshold
Increased telemetry cost due to per-tenant time-series - mitigated by aggregation and active-tenant sampling
Model quality regressions when falling back to quantized variants - requires product signoff and gated experiments
